cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Not Until You Explain
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I sign: our wedding invitation says Friday; your booking says Monday. Which document needs correcting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The invitation. Monday saved a fortune. I've got to get to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A changed booking needs a changed invitation. Stay here while we establish who has the wrong date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone. I thought we'd tell them after you signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the signature waits. Before we correct their invitations, explain why you thought signing could replace telling me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats a wedding-date contradiction as a document correction. A3 supervises notification and A5 rejects signature-first disclosure, using competence to make B explain the omission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cheaper-date answer leads A3 to ask who needs correction. B4 reveals the plan to delay telling guests until A signs; A5 withholds that same signature and asks why telling A was skipped.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a financial saving and to reach work; B4 discloses an ill-judged plan. A has a concrete shared decision at stake rather than abstract procedural authority.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from correcting guest information to demanding accountability for B4's treatment of A's own consent.

specificity.evidence: A1 now names the wedding and A as signer. B4 repeats A's signing role, eliminating the draft's ambiguous change of signer.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 holds the signature and asks one explanatory question. It does not add a new prop or conclude with a detached bureaucracy joke.
